content_units: Ontario Tenant Deposit Recovery Snapshot

This is general legal information for Ontario, not a final legal ruling. Based on your facts, the main issue is whether the landlord can keep   CAD 900   from a   last-month rent deposit   for cleaning, repainting, and blinds when you say the condition was ordinary wear and tear.
Practical Next Steps and Tenant Rights Checklist
Context used for this checklist
- Last-month rent deposit paid at move-in:   CAD 2,400
- Written non-renewal notice sent:   2024-07-01
- You moved out and returned keys:   2024-08-31
- Landlord claimed on   2024-09-10   they would keep   CAD 900
- Claimed reasons:   wall repainting, carpet cleaning, replacing two blinds
- You report   no major damage beyond normal wear
What to gather now
Option 1: Move-out evidence file   Build one clean package showing condition at move-out and handover   Most important proof
Gather photos
Option 2: Payment and deposit records   Keep the lease, deposit receipt, rent ledger, and proof deposit was for last month   Shows what the money was for
Organize records
Option 3: Notice and key-return proof   Save your 2024-07-01 notice, key return messages, and landlord email from 2024-09-10   Confirms timeline
Save emails
Option 4: Condition comparison notes   Make a short room-by-room list: walls, carpet, blinds, appliances, fixtures   Helps distinguish wear from damage
Prepare notes
Records to gather
- Signed lease and any renewal/non-renewal emails
- Proof of the   CAD 2,400   last-month rent deposit
- Your written notice sent on   2024-07-01
- Proof you vacated on   2024-08-31
- Proof keys were returned
- Move-in photos/videos, if any
- Move-out photos/videos, especially walls, carpet, window coverings
- Any inspection reports or walkthrough notes
- The landlord’s   2024-09-10   email
- Any invoices, estimates, or photos the landlord provided
- Screenshots of all text messages and emails
- A short timeline of events with dates
Key Ontario tenant-rights issues to check
- A   last-month rent deposit   is generally for rent, not a general damage fund.
- Ordinary   wear and tear   is usually different from tenant-caused damage.
- Items like   repainting between tenancies  , routine   cleaning  , or refresh work may not automatically be chargeable to a tenant.
- If the landlord says there was actual damage, they should be able to point to specific damage and supporting evidence.
- If the landlord wants compensation for damage, the dispute may need to be decided through the proper legal process rather than by simply deducting from a rent deposit.
- You may also want to check whether any   deposit interest   issue applies under Ontario rules for rent deposits.
Practical sequence to follow
- Send a firm written demand first and keep it concise.
- Ask for the   CAD 900   back and request any supporting invoices, photos, or move-out inspection record if they claim actual damage.
- Give a clear deadline:   14 days from the date of the letter  .
- Keep communication in writing only if possible.
- If they do not repay or give a satisfactory explanation, consider escalation through the   Landlord and Tenant Board   or legal help resources.
Sample Demand Letter for Return of Withheld Deposit Amount
Subject:   Request for return of CAD 900 withheld from last-month rent deposit
[Date]
[Landlord Name]
[Landlord Email or Mailing Address]
Dear [Landlord Name],

I rented the condo at [rental address] under a 12-month lease from   September 1, 2023 to August 31, 2024  . At move-in, I paid a   CAD 2,400 last-month rent deposit  . On   July 1, 2024  , I gave written notice that I would not renew the tenancy, and I moved out on   August 31, 2024   and returned the keys.
On   September 10, 2024  , you advised by email that you intended to keep   CAD 900   from my deposit for wall repainting, carpet cleaning, and replacing two blinds.

I dispute that deduction. To my knowledge, there was no damage beyond normal wear and tear when I moved out. In Ontario, a last-month rent deposit is not generally meant to be used as a repair or cleaning fund, and ordinary wear and tear is not the tenant’s responsibility in the same way as undue or wilful damage.

Please return the withheld   CAD 900   within   14 days   of the date of this letter, by [e-transfer / cheque / other payment method]. If you believe any deduction is justified, please send me, within the same 14-day period, all documents you rely on, including:
- photos of the alleged damage,
- move-in and move-out inspection records,
- invoices or receipts,
- and any explanation showing why the claimed costs are beyond normal wear and tear.

If I do not receive payment or a satisfactory response within 14 days, I will consider taking the next steps available to me, including seeking information about filing an application with the   Landlord and Tenant Board   and pursuing any other remedies available.
I hope we can resolve this promptly and professionally.
Sincerely,
[Your full name]
[Your phone number]
[Your email address]
[Forwarding address, if desired]
When to Escalate to the Landlord and Tenant Board
Consider escalating if:
- The landlord ignores your letter after   14 days
- The landlord refuses to return the   CAD 900
- The landlord gives only vague reasons and no proof
- The landlord insists they can automatically apply a rent deposit to cleaning or ordinary wear items
Before filing, make sure you have:
- Your timeline
- The lease and deposit proof
- Written notice proof
- Move-out evidence
- The landlord’s deduction email
- A copy of your demand letter and proof you sent it
